title: Machine-readable copy of product pages
question: Can an agent get a product page as Markdown instead of HTML?
method: GET a sampled product page with Accept: text/markdown, text/html;q=0.9. Pass when the response is text/markdown and names the product (warn when Vary: Accept is missing, because shared caches then serve Markdown to browsers). Also pass when the HTML links a Markdown alternate (link rel=alternate type=text/markdown) or the page URL with .md appended answers text/markdown. Fail when none applies. Coding agents request Markdown today; search crawlers do not, hence the low weight.

spec.title: Vercel: make your documentation readable by AI agents

title: Server-rendered product content
question: Are title, price and description present in the raw HTML without JavaScript?
method: Parse the raw HTML of sampled product pages. Pass when a title, a price-like value and a description are present as text or structured data; fail when the body is an empty app shell.

title: Page weight and response time
question: Is a product page small and fast enough to be fetched whole?
method: Measure the HTML bytes and the response time of sampled product pages (the home page when none). Pass under 1 MB and 3 seconds; warn under 2 MB and 8 seconds; fail above. Googlebot reads only the first 2 MB of a file; other crawlers publish no limits, so the thresholds are conservative hygiene, not a documented cut-off, and the weight is low.

spec.title: Googlebot and the first 2 MB of a file

title: Canonical and hreflang present
question: Can an agent tell which URL is the product's canonical one?
method: Pass when sampled product pages carry a rel=canonical that resolves to the same origin; warn when hreflang alternates exist for some but not all detected languages.

title: Accessible main content
question: Is the product content inside a main landmark and not hidden behind an overlay in the HTML?
method: Pass when a main or article landmark wraps the product content; warn when a consent overlay appears to wrap or precede it in the DOM.

title: Unknown URLs answer 404
question: Does the site tell an agent honestly when a page does not exist?
method: GET a random path under the origin that cannot exist. Pass on 404 or 410, whatever the body. Warn on a redirect to the home page. Fail when the server answers 200 with an HTML page (a soft 404): an agent then reads a page that does not exist as if it did, and every stale link it follows looks like content.

spec.title: Google: HTTP status codes, network and DNS errors (soft 404)
